sections.label: Elderly parent Tribunal applications
sections.summary: Applications by elderly parents to the Tribunal dropped from 183 in 2010 to 110 in the first year and stabilised at about 30 cases a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As I mentioned at my Second Reading speech on 9 May, the number of elderly parents who applied to the Tribunal had dropped significantly from 183 in 2010 to 110 within the first year of implementation and the number of applications has since stabilised at about 30 cases a year.

sections.label: MPA amendments balance and misuse
sections.summary: The amendments aim to balance strengthening provisions for parents with measures to prevent misuse of the MPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The current amendments before us require us to strike the right balance in strengthening provisions for parents, while introducing measures to prevent misuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: That is, we propose to amend the MPA to first, enhance Tribunal/Commissioner's powers in ensuring neglected elderly parents are adequately supported and to put in place new processes to prevent misuse of the MPA by those who did not fulfil their parental duties.

sections.label: Consultations and amendment outcomes
sections.summary: After focus groups, surveys and stakeholder deliberations, four key and three operational amendments were settled on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Through 13 focus group discussions with more than 200 participants, 1,000-over survey respondents on our preliminary ideas and after deliberating the various views with relevant stakeholders including the Tribunal and Commissioner, we landed on four key and three operational amendments.

sections.label: Parents with abandonment records permission
sections.summary: Parents with records of abandonment, abuse or neglect against their child must first seek the Tribunal's permission before proceeding with their claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The first key amendment involves parents with records of abandonment, abuse or neglect against their child that they must now first seek the Tribunal's permission before proceeding with their claim.

sections.label: Abandonment abuse neglect case proportions
sections.summary: About one in four Commissioner cases and one in three Tribunal cases involved persons alleging abandonment, abuse or neglect by their parent when young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Currently, about one in four cases at the Office of the Commissioner and one in three cases at the Tribunal involved persons who alleged abandonment, abuse or neglect by their parent when they were young.

sections.label: Workgroup proposal Tribunal permission
sections.summary: The workgroup proposes requiring parents with records of abuse, neglect or abandonment against their child to first seek the Tribunal's permission before proceeding with their claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: My workgroup proposes that we require parents with records of abuse, neglect or abandonment against their child to first seek the Tribunal's permission before proceeding with their claim.

sections.label: Tribunal permission for parent
sections.summary: The Tribunal may grant permission if the parent shows a good arguable case on abandonment, abuse, neglect or just and equitable grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Third, the Tribunal may grant permission if the parent showed a good arguable case that they did not abandon, abuse or neglect the child or that the child should maintain the parent on just and equitable grounds.

sections.label: Protections for unreported abandoned children
sections.summary: Consultation participants asked for protections to extend to children abandoned, abused or neglected by parents without official records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In both rounds of public consultation that we conducted, a sizable number of participants had asked for protections to be extended to children who have been abandoned, abused or neglected by their parents, but who do not have official records because the incidents were never reported.

sections.label: Dismissing frivolous or vexatious variations
sections.summary: The proposal allows the President or Deputy President to dismiss frivolous or vexatious variations, and the Tribunal to dismiss such applications without involving the respondent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And this can cause potential inefficiencies and delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, we propose to allow frivolous or vexatious variations to be dismissed by the President or a Deputy President, similar to fresh applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We propose to also allow the Tribunal, as well as the President or a Deputy President of the Tribunal to dismiss an application that is deemed to be frivolous or vexatious without informing or involving the respondent.

sections.label: Commissioner's conciliation for elderly parents
sections.summary: The moderated proposal empowers the Commissioner on his own motion to have children attend conciliation about care arrangements and their legal obligation to support parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some focus group participants also raised concern over the emotional distress that the Commissioner's application might cause to the parent, since it would be going against his wish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have accordingly moderated the proposal, to only empower Commissioner on his own motion, that is, not at the parent's behest, to have their children attend conciliation at the Commissioner's Office so that care arrangements for the parent can be discussed and the children can be reminded that they have the legal obligation to support their elderly parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The proposed section 12B empowers the Commissioner to do this.

sections.label: Tribunal non-monetary directions
sections.summary: The fourth key amendment empowers the Tribunal to make non-monetary directions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Our fourth and final key amendment is to empower the Tribunal to make non-monetary directions.

sections.label: Non-monetary directions and gambling counselling
sections.summary: The Tribunal may make non-monetary directions furthering section 6(6) purposes, and require parents with problem-gambling issues to attend gambling counselling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There have been multiple cases where the children were unwilling to pay maintenance simply because they were aware of the problem gambling-related issues in the parent and are worried that the parent would gamble away the maintenance they received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We thus propose to allow the Tribunal to make any non-monetary direction that it deems fit, if the direction is one that furthers one of the purposes under the new section 6(6), which include the exercise of financial responsibility by the parent or child and the management or resolution of conflicts between the parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In cases where the Tribunal finds that the parent has issues related to problem-gambling, it can require the parent to attend gambling counselling.

sections.label: Definition of child clarified
sections.summary: The review proposes operational amendments, clarifying that "child" in section 2 means adult children aged 21 or above, to prevent minors from being subject to claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the course of our review, we are also proposing various operational amendments to enhance efficacy of the Act and to streamline processes, and these are as follows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We clarify the definition of "child" in section 2 of the Act as adult children aged 21 or above, and this is to prevent minors from being subject to claims.

sections.label: MPA sends strong signal
sections.summary: The speaker says public funds would otherwise be expended due to problems within private relationships, and the MPA sends a strong signal of what is stood against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, I would not even have ventured this far, had it not been the fact that public funds would have to be otherwise expended due to the problems within these private relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And that is, the MPA also serves to send a strong signal of what we stand against.

sections.label: Tribunal permission circumstances
sections.summary: The Tribunal's permission will be needed in three circumstances as provided for in the proposed section 3B in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Tribunal's permission will be needed in the following three circumstances as provided for in the proposed section 3B in the Bill.

sections.label: Permission good arguable case
sections.summary: Permission may be granted if there is a good arguable case at two levels: the parent did not commit ANA, or the child should still maintain the parent on just and equitable grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In essence, it is provided that permission may be granted if there is a good arguable case at two levels: first, that the parent did not commit ANA; or second, the child should still maintain the parent on just and equitable grounds.

sections.label: Applicant better of argument
sections.summary: The reasoning of a 2018 Court of Appeal decision was adopted, meaning the applicant should have the better of the argument, a threshold above prima facie but below balance of probabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Here, we adopted the reasoning in a 2018 Court of Appeal decision and intend that it means that the applicant should have the better of the argument.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This threshold is more than a "prima facie" case, but lower than that of a balance of probabilities.

sections.label: Appeal against permission refusal
sections.summary: Proposed section 18(3A) provides that an appeal may be brought against the Tribunal's decision not to grant permission to the General Division of the High Court, with no appeal contemplated where permission is granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 18(3A) in the Bill, it is provided that an appeal may be brought against the Tribunal's decision not to grant permission to the General Division of the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Whilst not expressly stated, this also means is that, subject to the High Court's powers under written law, including sections 16 and 17 of the Act, there is no appeal contemplated against the decision of the Tribunal where permission is granted for a parent to apply for maintenance.

sections.label: Bill procedure under section 8
sections.summary: The Bill provides a procedure for them under the proposed section 8.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill provides a procedure for them under the proposed section 8 in the Bill.

sections.label: Tribunal power to vary maintenance order
sections.summary: The Tribunal may vary or rescind a maintenance order if satisfied of a parent's previously unconsidered ANA record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Tribunal, should it be satisfied that the parent has a record of ANA that was not previously considered at the time when the maintenance order was made, will have the power to vary or rescind the maintenance order.

sections.label: Gag order information access safeguards
sections.summary: Safeguards limit the Commissioner's and Tribunal's access to gag order protected information to ascertaining if a parent has an ANA record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In a situation where the parent whose identity is protected by a gag order, subsequently applies for maintenance from a child, it is necessary to provide the Commissioner and the Tribunal, which are quasi-judicial bodies, access to information that may be relevant to establishing if the parents have records of ANA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For these reasons, safeguards have been provided to limit the purpose of access to information protected by the gag order to only for the purposes of ascertaining if the parent has a record of ANA.

sections.label: Moral basis of duties
sections.summary: The law is clear that the moral basis for such duties rests on whether the parent fulfilled a minimum level of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Here, the law is quite clear that the moral basis for the existence of such duties rests on whether the parent has fulfilled a minimum level of care.

sections.label: Not a very bad parent
sections.summary: One need not be a good parent, merely not a very bad one, to make claims on a child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In short, one does not have to be a good parent, merely not a very bad one, to be able to make claims on a child.

sections.label: Consultations and survey conducted
sections.summary: Meetings, 13 focus group discussions, public consultation and a survey of 1,000 respondents were conducted on supporting parents and the proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In addition to our meetings with the Tribunal President, Deputy Presidents and the Commissioner, 13 focus group discussions and public consultation held over REACH's online portal, we also conducted a survey with 1,000 respondents to understand the prevailing broad values towards supporting parents in their elderly years, opinions towards the proposed amendments and general awareness of and familiarity with the Maintenance of Parents Act.

sections.label: Broadening Act to non-monetary means
sections.summary: Since the Act came into force, close to 2,500 applications were received, around 90% resolved through mediation, and the Act's scope must be broadened to include non-monetary means.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Since the Act came into force, close to 2,500 applications have been received.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Around 90% of the applications were resolved through mediation, avoiding further acrimony between the elderly and their offspring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: After months of review, we came to a few conclusions: Firstly, the scope of the Act must be broadened to include non-monetary means to improve relations between the elderly and their offspring and encourage them to re-connect.

sections.label: Empowering Commissioner for mediation only
sections.summary: The workgroup believes amendments are necessary to protect family values and empower the Commissioner to contact children solely for mediation, not to ask for maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: After rounds of deliberation, the workgroup believes that amendments are necessary to protect our family values, and empower the Commissioner to contact the children, but solely for mediation purposes, not to ask for maintenance, so as to preserve the relationship.

sections.label: Non-monetary orders and conditional approvals
sections.summary: The amendment Bill will authorise the Tribunal to issue non-monetary Court orders or approve maintenance applications with conditions, such as mandatory counselling for the parent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For such cases, the children's refusal to pay maintenance to avoid feeding the bad habit is understandable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, this amendment Bill will authorise the Tribunal to issue non-monetary Court orders, or approve the maintenance application with conditions, for example, requiring the parent to go for mandatory counselling.

sections.label: Commissioner access to child abuse records
sections.summary: The amendment Bill will empower the Commissioner to access Government files to check for records of child abuse by the applicant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: After all, filial piety should be based on parental love in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, this amendment Bill will empower the Commissioner to access Government files, to check for records of child abuse by the applicant.

sections.label: Tribunal power to reject applications
sections.summary: The amendment Bill will empower the Tribunal to directly reject applications under certain circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Despite being rejected, they continue to reapply repeatedly, intentionally causing frustrations to their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, this amendment Bill will empower the Tribunal to directly reject applications under certain circumstances.

sections.label: Safeguards, reconciliation and family values
sections.summary: The Government will assist children in genuine financial difficulty, but the Act safeguards against irresponsible children, allows deserving parents to obtain maintenance, offers estranged families a chance to reconcile, and re-affirms family values.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: After all, as the age-old saying goes "Filial piety is a virtue to be held above all else, but what is important is the heart and not the action, if one only looks at actions, then there will be no filial sons." If the children face genuine financial difficulties, of course, the Government will have to step in to provide assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But we have to safeguard against irresponsible children who believe that the Government will not deny help to their parents, those who wilfully abandon their parents and expect others to shoulder their responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One will not become filial just because of the Maintenance of Parents Act, but the Act will allow deserving parents to obtain maintenance and provide estranged family members with a chance to reconcile.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: At the same time, it re-affirms society's emphasis on family values, while ensuring that children who have been harmed are fairly treated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill is the result of more than 20 years of experience, and a synthesis of collective wisdom.

sections.label: Balancing child protection and elderly access
sections.summary: Asks how to balance protecting children from parents' claims with fair justice access for elderly parents when no records exist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How do we strike a balance between protecting these children from claims from their parents and ensuring fair access to justice for elderly parents in cases where no records exist?

sections.label: Tribunal trauma-informed practices
sections.summary: The Tribunal and Commissioner overseeing parents' maintenance have implemented trauma-informed practices to manage and minimise distress for children involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Tribunal and Commissioner, responsible for overseeing the maintenance of parents, have implemented trauma-informed practices to manage and minimise distress for the children involved.

sections.label: Extended family support claims rejected
sections.summary: Broadening support claims to grandparents, aunts, uncles and extended family was determined to pose practical challenges, after considering effects on grandparents and grandchildren.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This was seriously taken into account, as was the possible influence on both grandparents and grandchildren.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, after careful consideration, it was determined that broadening the scope of support claims to include grandparents, aunts, uncles and other extended family members would pose practical challenges, as also highlighted by my hon colleague Ms Tin Pei Ling.

sections.label: Decision against expanding claim scope
sections.summary: Scope was not expanded because it would create practical challenges, hinder enforcement, burden the system and trouble families; an amendment protects children from harrowing processes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: After much consideration, we decided not to expand the scope because that would create practical challenges and could make it more difficult to enforce the Act, burden the system and create trouble for families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As a member of the workgroup on this Bill, I would like to share my thought process and concerns regarding two amendments in the Bill and how it evolved along the way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that a trauma-informed approach underpins this proposed amendment to prevent abandoned or abused children from being approached at all, if there are records of such treatment that the state is aware of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It would unnecessarily induce damaging feelings of self-doubt, guilt or worsen feelings of resentment, when they may have spent years trying to heal or to move on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, we have put up this amendment that seeks to protect these children from an unnecessary and harrowing process only to have the case dismissed in the end.

sections.label: Counselling support and Commissioner conciliation
sections.summary: Counselling and therapy services are available to support respondents giving accounts to the Tribunal; amendment three lets the Commissioner initiate conciliation without parental consent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In raising my concern during the Workgroup meetings and in talks with MSF on our proposed Bill, I understand from MSF colleagues that counselling and therapy services are, in fact, available and provided if needed, to support respondents who are asked to come forward to give their account and to share their stories to the Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, is amendment three that empowers the Commissioner to initiate conciliation without consent from the parent.

sections.label: Elderly leaving assets to children
sections.summary: Many elderly residents plan to leave assets to their children, shown by low take-up of the Lease Buyback scheme for HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many elderly residents continue to plan on leaving their assets to their children, for example, in the low take-up rates for the Lease Buyback scheme for their HDB flats, so that they have something to leave behind for their children even when they pass on.

sections.label: Commissioner claiming maintenance from children
sections.summary: The original amendment three would let the Commissioner claim maintenance from financially able children on behalf of neglected and destitute parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The original proposal for amendment three allows for the Commissioner to claim maintenance from financially able children on behalf of the neglected and destitute parents and it presents exactly this dilemma.

sections.label: Revised conciliation and Tribunal amendments
sections.summary: The revised proposal empowers the Commissioner to have children attend conciliation, and other amendments allow non-monetary directions and dismissal of frivolous applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The outcome and revised proposal – to empower the Commissioner on his own motion and not at the parent's behest to have the children attend conciliation at the Commissioner's Office so that care arrangements can be discussed and their children can be reminded of their legal obligations – is a great balanced approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In considering that preserving a good relationship between parent and child is the utmost priority in the elderly parents' minds, we have to ensure that we do no harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, what we really need to ensure is in the implementation, that the communication to children being asked to come forward for conciliation, knows that the request is being made by the Commissioner and not by the parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The other two amendments which allow for the Tribunal to give non-monetary directions for cases and for the Tribunal to dismiss frivolous and vexatious applications are relatively straightforward to me.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They are enhancements to the Act made with 12 years of experience in consultation with the relevant agencies since it was last reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I am satisfied that they are appropriate enhancements made in the spirit of fairness to both parent and children as well as to ensure that public resources are not frivolously frittered away.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that my concerns for amendments one and three have been adequately addressed in our workgroup's development of the Bill, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Amendments addressing abuse and neglect
sections.summary: Proposed amendments require records of abuse, abandonment or neglect to be considered, allow dismissal of frivolous applications, and provide financial and non-monetary directions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This ensured that seniors and their children attempted to kind of resolve their differences amicably before resorting to legal measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And consequently, the number of applications at the Tribunal significantly reduced to about 30 per year, signalling the success of this approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, it has been reported that one in three cases seen at the Tribunal involve allegations that the parents had previously abused, abandoned or neglected their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The second development was that there have been cases of errant children who leave their elderly parents in care facilities, expecting the facility management to care for, to raise funds and to bear the financial burden of their parents' maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, the latest round of proposed amendments aims to address these key issues and also introduce ways to improve effectiveness of the MPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They include provisions that require records of abuse, abandonment or neglect to be considered before parents can seek maintenance orders, it also involves dismissal of frivolous and vexatious applications; and directions of financial and/or non-monetary measures; amongst others.

sections.label: Elderly population and maintenance amounts
sections.summary: By 2030 about 22% of residents will be 65 and above, and from 2016 to 2020, 82% of Tribunal awards were under $500 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Most of us know that by 2030, approximately 22%, or at least one in five of the resident population will be 65 years and above, with nearly one in three elderly persons in Singapore forecasted to require eldercare services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We found out that many who regularly provide for their elderly parents can only afford a monthly allowance of $500 or less, this quantum is also reflected similarly in maintenance orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2020, 82% of awards that are granted by the Tribunal had a monthly quantum of less than $500.

sections.label: Government provisions for seniors
sections.summary: Government and societal provisions include raising the Retirement Age, CPF Life, Silver Support, CareShield, HDB schemes and Public Assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A slew of Government and societal provisions has been introduced to meet these needs, and work is still in progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: These include: raising of Retirement Age so that those who wish to continue to work can choose to do so; CPF Life Annuity Scheme; Silver Support Scheme; CareShield; HDB's Rental Scheme, Housing Leaseback Scheme and Assisted Community Care Apartments and Public Assistance Scheme for seniors who qualify for long-term financial assistance from MSF.

sections.label: Supporting Tribunal and Commissioner powers
sections.summary: The speaker supports boosting the Tribunal's and Commissioner's powers to support neglected elderly parents, and asks about preventing past abusers from misusing the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Such conversations should be approached with sensitivity, recognising the unique circumstances and financial capabilities of each family member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the amendment to the Act to boost the powers of the Tribunal for the Maintenance of Parents and the Commissioner for the Maintenance of Parents so that neglected elderly parents are adequately supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As for the amendment to prevent parents who have abused, abandoned or neglected their children in the past from misusing the Maintenance of Parents Act, I have a question.

sections.label: Partial support from children
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would accord a parent some partial support from his children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry accord the parent some partial support from his children?

sections.label: Ministry mediating for fairness
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will help to mediate for fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry help to mediate for fairness?

sections.label: Child Protective Services case numbers
sections.summary: The passage states investigated cases rose from 381 in 2014 to 2,141 in 2021, and MSF's explanation for the increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2014, 381 cases were investigated by MSF's Child Protective Services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2021, this figure soared to 2,141, the highest in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MSF explained that the number of cases has increased since 2015 when MSF introduced more rigorous screening tools and training for professionals.

sections.label: Standard of proof for abuse cases
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the standard of proof for pre-2015 child abuse cases can be adjusted for under-reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Member share whether the standard of proof for pre-2015 child abuse cases be adjusted to take into account the potential issue of under-reporting?

sections.label: Tribunal's additional powers under amendment
sections.summary: The passage states the amendment gives the Tribunal discretion for non-monetary orders and power to subject maintenance payment to conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the proposed amendment, the Tribunal will have two additional powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One, the Tribunal have the discretion to give direction for appropriate non-monetary orders according to each family's unique circumstance where necessary; and two, the Tribunal will be allowed to subject the maintenance payment to compliance with the non-monetary order or with other specified conditions, such as attendance or completion of counselling sessions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These amendments will allow the Tribunal to have more options to address fundamental family issues to improve approval and compliance of the maintenance orders.

sections.label: Powers over addicted parents
sections.summary: The passage states the amendment Bill gives greater powers to compel addicted parents to undergo counselling and mend family ties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many addiction problems are longstanding, causing family tensions and distrust between parents and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, the amendment Bill will give the Commissioner for the Maintenance of Parents and the Tribunal for the Maintenance of Parents greater powers to compel addicted parents to undergo counselling and to mend their family ties through counselling.

sections.label: Non-monetary maintenance orders
sections.summary: The amendment lets the Commissioner and Tribunal order non-monetary maintenance so children can maintain parents without being exploited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, the amendment also enables the Commissioner and the Tribunal to order non-monetary maintenance to allow children to maintain their parents without being exploited.

sections.label: Balancing elderly care and child protection
sections.summary: The MPA amendments aim to balance neglected elderly parents' access to support with safeguards against misuse by parents who failed their obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Society must continue to balance between ensuring elderly parents having access to justice and care while protecting abused children from facing distress and having to deal with their traumatic childhood experiences due to neglect from their parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The MPA amendments aim to achieve such a balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Bill's proposed amendments will therefore serve to better ensure that neglected elderly parents are adequately supported while placing safeguards to prevent the misuse of the MPA by those who did not adequately fulfil their parental obligations.

sections.label: Locating children for mandatory conciliation
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Commissioner to locate destitute parents' children for mandatory conciliation without a formal application by the parent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: One of the key amendments of the Bill is to empower the Commissioner to locate the children of destitute parents for mandatory conciliation without a need for the parent to put in a formal application.

sections.label: Tribunal discretion for non-monetary orders
sections.summary: The Tribunal may make non-monetary orders in the parent's interest, set maintenance conditions, and withhold children's maintenance obligation if conditions are unmet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Bill therefore proposes to give the Tribunal the discretion to make non-monetary orders if it is in the interest of the parent at hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Tribunal will be allowed to set conditions on the payment of maintenance and if the parent does not comply with the non-monetary order, then the children will not be obligated to pay maintenance.

sections.label: Conciliation process and proposed changes
sections.summary: Conciliation could have helped Mdm C, has a 90% resolution rate, and proposed changes include non-monetary orders like counselling for addicted parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For Mdm C, a conciliation process could have circumvented the sting of a Court tribunal settlement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is heartening to note that the conciliation process has achieved a 90% resolution rate since its implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One, train mediators in financial counselling so that they can equip children on sustainable maintenance payments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Two, create a direct appeal line to the HDB on expedited rental or long-term lease alternatives via the conciliation platform.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And three, I note that one of the proposed changes is to allow the Tribunal to introduce non-monetary orders such as requiring parents with addictions to attend counselling.

sections.label: Discretion, reconciliation and counselling conditions
sections.summary: The Tribunal may deny abusive parents support eligibility, reconciliation is the first step, and parents with gambling habits may be required to undergo counselling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment accords the Tribunal the discretion to deny the parents of the Maintenance Agreement's eligibility for support if there is sufficient evidence to suggest that the parents have abused the children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is very good that the amendment Bill has also set out a framework to step up reconciliation as the first step.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is also important that in the implementation of the maintenance order, the Tribunal can require the beneficiaries, that is, the parents, to undergo counselling if the parents are found to have, for example, gambling habits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the balance, the amendment also gives the Government the discretion to directly reach out to children who have the means to provide and care for their parents' basic needs but have abandoned their parents to destitute homes, expecting the taxpayers to pick up the tab.

sections.label: Family service centres conciliatory efforts
sections.summary: Asks whether recommended amendment processes engage family service centres for conciliatory efforts before the Government reaches out to children without consent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the amendment processes recommended engage the family service centres to attempt conciliatory efforts first before taking amendment 3, involving the Government directly reaching out to the children of the destitute parents without consent?

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I echo Member Carrie Tan's caution to be sensitive in the communications' approach and the language used with the children to ensure that we do not do more harm to already estranged relationships.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The Member states that notwithstanding the clarifications, she supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Defining sufficiently serious abuse
sections.summary: The Member says it is critical to clarify what constitutes sufficiently serious abuse to exempt an individual from the Bill's responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, it is critical that we clarify what constitutes sufficiently serious abuse to exempt an individual from the responsibilities outlined in this Bill.

sections.label: Clause 4 and parents' destitution
sections.summary: The Member says clause 4 raises important questions about the circumstances that led to the parents' destitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mdm Deputy Speaker, clause 4 raises important questions regarding the circumstances that led to the parents' destitution.

sections.label: Tribunal determining reasonable support amount
sections.summary: The Member says the Tribunal must determine a reasonable amount to support parents and prevent excessive claims, including for the sandwich class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, we must consider how the Tribunal will determine a reasonable amount to support these parents, particularly to prevent any potentially excessive claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This becomes even more significant when considering the sandwich class, who may already face challenges in raising their own children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is important to strike a balance that ensures adequate support for the parents while avoiding any abuse of the system.

sections.label: Weakened family ties and education
sections.summary: The Member says the Bill does not address weakening family ties and calls for early education on honouring parents and bidirectional love and respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, the notion of "perfect families" where the responsibility of supporting aged parents is equitably distributed is a rarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This legislation may be perceived as an unfortunate necessity, acknowledging the sad reality that extreme cases of elder neglect or abuse do exist in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Similarly, the state also has the responsibility to provide justice for the individuals who have suffered at the hands of their parents, which some of the amendments in this Bill addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, it is important to recognise that this Bill does not address the underlying issue at its core, the weakening family ties and the diminished perception amongst children regarding the importance of reciprocating their parents' love and care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One key focus area must be the reinforcement of education from an early age to honour parents and for parents to understand that love and respect are bi-directional.

sections.label: Reducing strained family relationships
sections.summary: This reduces the likelihood of strained relationships that require legal intervention such as the Maintenance of Parents Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In doing so, we reduce the likelihood of strained relationships that necessitate legal intervention in the likes of the Maintenance of Parents Act.

sections.label: Maintenance of Parents cases and support
sections.summary: CMP cases fell from 303 in 2012 to 110 in 2022, while elderly receive Government support through Pioneer and Merdeka Generation packages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2022, a total of 110 cases were submitted to the Commissioner for the Maintenance of Parents (CMP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This figure has dropped from 303 cases in 2012, the highest level over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Our elderly also receives more support from the Government through schemes, such as the Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation packages, which, among other things, offer additional subsidies for healthcare.

sections.label: Support for amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker states support for the amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, I support the amendment Bill.

sections.label: Survey findings on family support
sections.summary: Surveys found most elderly have close-knit families and can rely on married children for physical, emotional and financial support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From MSF's 2019 Survey on the Social Attitudes of Singaporeans, 93% of elderly respondents stated that they have a close-knit family and 96% aged between 15 and 64 agreed that it is their duty to take care of their parents, regardless of their qualities or faults.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Similarly, from HDB's Sample Household 2018 survey, 71% of elderly aged 65 and above were able to rely on their married children for physical support, 95% for emotional support and 90% for financial support in times of need.

sections.label: Ageing population by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be 65 or older, with 83,000 living alone and 100,000 needing ADL help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be 65 and older.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: An estimated 83,000 seniors will live alone and some 100,000 seniors will need help with at least one Activity of Daily Living (ADL).

sections.label: Commissioner acting in glaring cases
sections.summary: The speaker agrees that in glaring cases the Commissioner should act without the parent initiating the process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Hands were tied and nothing else could be done to take them to task.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: I agree that in such glaring cases, the Commissioner should be allowed to act without needing the parent to initiate the process.

sections.label: Commissioner intervention as last resort
sections.summary: The amendment lets the Commissioner intervene only as a last resort after the welfare home exhausts other options and specific beliefs are met.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Workgroup has emphasised that the amendment is intended for the Commissioner to intervene only as a last resort, after the welfare home has exhausted all other options and only if the Commissioner reasonably believes that the parent has no records of abandonment, abuse or neglect, and that the children can afford the maintenance.

sections.label: Tribunal non-monetary directions for relationships
sections.summary: The amendment empowers the Tribunal to make non-monetary directions, such as counselling orders, to address issues straining family relationships and help repair them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For cases before the Tribunal, often the underlying cause of maintenance disputes is strained relationships.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This amendment empowers the Tribunal to make non-monetary directions, such as imposing counselling orders to address behavioural or emotional issues that strain family relationships, and help disputing family members take steps to repair their relationships.

sections.label: Conditional maintenance payments on counselling
sections.summary: The Tribunal may order maintenance payments conditional on the parent attending counselling, for example for gambling addiction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With this, the Tribunal may order that maintenance payments are conditional on the parent attending, for example, counselling for gambling addiction.

sections.label: Permission required with ANA records
sections.summary: Where official records of ANA exist, a parent cannot commence action against the child without Tribunal permission, to prevent re-traumatisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: What is proposed here is that where there is objective evidence in form of official records of ANA, then the parent cannot commence action against the child unless he gets permission of the Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The policy objective here is to prevent the child from being re-traumatised in situations where it is plain and obvious that parent would not be granted an order of maintenance on just and equitable grounds because of his record of ANA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is worth emphasising that in the focus group discussions that were organised, almost all participants who came from troubled family backgrounds were of the view that it would be better for them not to be told of their parents' application for permission at this stage.

sections.label: Standard of proof for parent
sections.summary: The standard of proof the parent must discharge is higher than a prima facie case but lower than a balance of probabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I explained in my earlier speech that the standard of proof that the parent has to discharge is not low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is higher than a "prima facie" case but lower than a case made out on a balance of probabilities.

sections.label: Child participation in permission proceedings
sections.summary: The Bill provides the child an opportunity to participate in permission proceedings, and if permission is granted or no ANA record exists, the current system follows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Here the issue of wanting to prevent the child from re-traumatisation would be moot because he was already being put on notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is specifically provided in the Bill that the child in these circumstances would have an opportunity to participate in the proceedings to get permission —

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Where the Tribunal grants permission, or where there is no official record of parents' ANA, then the process that will follow is, in essence, equivalent of the current system.

sections.label: Child opposing parent maintenance application
sections.summary: A child can adduce evidence of a parent's abandonment, abuse or neglect to oppose the parent's maintenance application, and granting permission does not affect that ability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: By the time the permission is granted to the parent to bring a maintenance application against his child, the sieving process would have ended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As is provided for in the current system, he or she will be able to adduce evidence of the parents’ ANA of him or her in opposition to the parent's application for maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The Tribunal's decision to grant the parent permission to apply for maintenance does not impact on the ability of the child to oppose the maintenance application.

sections.label: Parent seeking support from some children
sections.summary: Mr Don Wee asked what happens if a parent has a few children but only seeks support from particular ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee asked what if the parent has a few children but only seeks support from particular ones.

sections.label: Leave of Tribunal for claims
sections.summary: Where there are official records of abandonment, abuse or neglect, the parent must first obtain the Tribunal's leave to proceed with the claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: For such a case, if there are official records of abandonment, abuse or neglect, then the parent will have to first obtain the leave of the Tribunal if he wants to proceed with his claim.

sections.label: Maintenance of parents legislation
sections.summary: Maintenance of parents legislation is not unique to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Actually, maintenance of parents legislation is not unique to Singapore.

sections.label: Commissioner initiating conciliation for children
sections.summary: The amendment is scoped to allow the Commissioner to initiate conciliation for children whose parents are in welfare homes or undergoing assessment for admission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: We need to reiterate clearly what we as a society expect of children, regardless of whether the parents have the desire to claim against their children or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: We have specifically scoped this amendment to allow the Commissioner to initiate conciliation for the children whose parents are in welfare homes or are undergoing assessment for admission.

sections.label: Abandonment, abuse or neglect cases
sections.summary: One in three cases at the Tribunal involve accounts of abandonment, abuse or neglect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: As I had mentioned before, one in three cases at the Tribunal involve such accounts of abandonment, abuse or neglect.

sections.label: Tribunal cases and abandonment
sections.summary: About one in three Tribunal cases involve abandonment, abuse or neglect; around 2,500 cases have come under the MPA since 1996.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: About one in three cases at the Tribunal involve accounts of abandonment, abuse or neglect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Ms Janet Ang asked about the number of cases that have come under the Act since it was first passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: There have been around 2,500 cases under the MPA since 1996.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: She also asked about the number of cases that will come under the new amendment and whether these would be dismissed if the amendments were in force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: We do expect that a sizable proportion of cases will not have official records of abuse, neglect or abandonment but many of them would likely be dismissed subsequently by the Tribunal when it hears the parties.

sections.label: Parents and schools shaping children
sections.summary: The issue is not addressed by this Bill or the MPA; parents and schools shape children, and families should have open conversations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: As Mr Yip mentioned, this issue is not addressed by this Bill or the MPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Both parents and schools have a role to play in shaping our children in the way they should go and I agree with Mr Don Wee that it is important for families to have open conversations about these matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: This is, of course, not just for the sake of the parent, but it will help the child to grow and to walk an honourable path in the community, being generous to others, instead of in isolation or individualism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: This is the hallmark of a truly great society, one which we can all be proud of as we also continue to refresh and to strengthen our social compact.

sections.label: Commissioner for Maintenance of Parents claims
sections.summary: Since March 2011, about 90% of claims referred annually to the Commissioner were settled at conciliation, and Tribunal applications dropped from 183 in 2010 to around 30 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Since its implementation in March 2011, about 90% of the claims referred annually to the Commissioner for the Maintenance of Parents were settled at conciliation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Consequently, the number of elderly parents who applied to the Tribunal has dropped significantly from 183 in 2010 to 110 within the first year of implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The applications dropped steadily over the years, have now stabilised and number at around 30 per year.

sections.label: Amending MPA to enhance powers
sections.summary: The proposal is to amend the MPA to enhance the powers of the Tribunal and the Commissioner in ensuring neglected elderly parents are adequately supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: First, we propose to amend the MPA to enhance the powers of the Tribunal and the Commissioner in ensuring that neglected elderly parents are adequately supported.
